strings.name: Al Gore
strings.role: Former US vice president · Climate advocate
strings.summary: Gore represented Tennessee in Congress before serving as US vice president from 1993 to 2001, focusing on the environment, information technology and government reform. He won the popular vote in 2000 but conceded after litigation over Florida’s recount. After office, his speeches, An Inconvenient Truth and organizational work promoted climate action. He shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: After serving as US vice president, he advanced global climate communication and action and shared the Nobel Peace Prize with the IPCC.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Harvard University, bachelor’s degree in government (1969)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Communicating climate science
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Used public talks and An Inconvenient Truth to broaden awareness of human-caused climate change.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Shared the Nobel Peace Prize
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Shared the 2007 prize with the IPCC for building and spreading knowledge about climate change.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Continued climate advocacy
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Discussed climate risks and the potential of renewable energy during New York Climate Week.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Shared the award with the IPCC for climate communication and laying foundations for action.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: An Inconvenient Truth released
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The documentary built around his climate presentation brought the issue to wider audiences.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Conceded the presidential election
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Conceded after the Supreme Court halted Florida’s recount, while expressing disagreement with the ruling.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became US vice president
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Elected alongside Bill Clinton and worked on government efficiency, technology and environmental policy.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Supported high-performance computing
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Sponsored legislation supporting high-performance computing and networking.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Entered the US Senate
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Moved from the House to the Senate and continued work on environmental, technology and defense issues.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Elected to the House
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Won a Tennessee congressional seat after working in journalism and took office the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Graduated and joined the Army
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Enlisted after graduating from Harvard and later served as a military journalist in Vietnam.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Washington
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Washington, DC, and raised between the capital and Tennessee.
